note:
Paul's verdict, read from Genesis: 'Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.' (Gen 15:6), which Paul quotes: 'Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness.' (Rom 4:3).

**Implied, not explicit.** Neither verse says 'justified by faith' of Abraham in those words; Paul reaches it by argument, and the phrase itself arrives at Rom 5:1. James's sentence is the explicit one: 'justified by what he did' (Jas 2:21).

Cited to these two verses since 2026-10-28. It cited Rom 4:2, a conditional Paul answers with 'but not before God' ('If Abraham was indeed justified by works'), and Heb 11:8, where he obeyed by faith and nothing is said of being justified.

The letter of James, on the binding of Isaac: 'justified by what he did when he offered his son Isaac on the altar' (Jas 2:21), and in James's own words 'his faith was working with his actions, and his faith was perfected by what he did' (2:22). Two verses later it quotes the same Old Testament sentence Paul quotes (Jas 2:23, Gen 15:6).

'The promises were spoken to Abraham and to his seed. The Scripture does not say, “and to seeds,” meaning many, but “and to your seed,” meaning One, who is Christ.' (Gal 3:16). **The key is given by arguing against a rival reading of the same word**, which is rare -- most identifications in the corpus are simply asserted.
Said 'to the Jews who had believed Him': 'If you continue in My word, you are truly My disciples' (John 8:31). An invitation, and John 8:30 says 'many believed in Him'.
scope_party: the Jews who had believed Him

note: 'Abraham is our father,' they replied. 'If you were children of Abraham,' said Jesus, 'you would do the works of Abraham' (John 8:39). The verse says 'they'; the nearest verse that names whom Jesus is speaking with is John 8:31, 'the Jews who had believed Him'. By 8:37 ('you are trying to kill Me') and 8:48 ('The Jews answered Him') the exchange has widened, and the text does not say whether 'they' is one group throughout.
scope_party: the Jews who had believed Him

note: Held. The verse says 'you' and names no group; it is spoken inside the exchange that begins at John 8:31 and has widened by 8:37, and the text does not say to whom within it. Kept in the data, printed in the John 8 passage as the verse reads, and filed on no group's card.

'We are Abraham's descendants,' they answered (John 8:33); 'I know you are Abraham's descendants' (John 8:37) -- Jesus grants the descent they claim at 8:33, and speaks to them of what follows from it: 'If you were children of Abraham, ... you would do the works of Abraham' (8:39). The verses say 'we' and 'you', which is why this is implied: the party is read back from John 8:31, and the claim is theirs, not the whole people's.
